newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's drops most of Campaign 55.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's drops most of Campaign 55.

text.p: McDonald's Corp., after posting disappointing U.S. sales in May, said Tuesday was dropping its Campaign 55 price promotion at lunch and dinner, a move that was applauded by several franchisees.

"I've been an operator for 13 years and this is the happiest day of my life," Bob Srygley, who operates four McDonald's franchises in Arkansas. "McDonald's is finally listening to the operators for a change."
McDonald's said it would drop Campaign 55 at lunch and dinner early next week although the Campaign will continue at breakfast.
Instead, McDonald's will go back to its existing Extra Value meal pricing, featuring sandwiches, french fries and a beverage starting at $2.99, said McDonald's spokesman Charles Ebeling.

Campaign 55, which was launched in early April, had been criticised by some franchisees who complained the price promotion hurt their sales and profit margins. Campaign 55 offered featured hamburgers for 55 cents when customers also purchased french fries and a drink.
The company had previously said increased store traffic would more than compensate for the reduction in the average customer check as a result of the lower price.
But based on May U.S. sales, Campaign 55 did not deliver the expected sales gain, financial analysts said.
U.S. same store sales in May -- measuring results for units open at least a year -- fell by about 5 percent, McDonald's franchisees sources said.
"Results were abysmal," a West Coast franchisee said. "The company saw no light at the end of the tunnel."
McDonald's said the change in Campaign 55 was in response to feedback from franchisees and customers.
McDonald's admitted that the customer response to Campaign 55 at lunch and dinner was "not up to our expectations."
McDonald's, however, is continuing with the 55 cents promotion at breakfast. Under that offer, breakfast sandwiches are priced at 55 cents when a customer also buys hash browns and a drink.
McDonald's said customer response to Campaign 55 breakfast meals was outstanding.
"Nationally, it worked," Srygley said of the breakfast campaign.
Ebeling said that McDonald's will support the breakfast campaign with increased national adverstising.
Franchisees said they were surprised at how quickly the Oak Brook, Ill.-based fast food chain had changed Campaign 55, which it had aggressively promoted to its U.S. operators.
McDonald's, however, said in its statement, "We made it clear from the start that we would monitor performance closely and make adjustments along the way as needed.
